claims.text: Al0.35CoCrFeNi or similar Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni compositions can have an FCC+BCC dual-phase constitution.
Cast Al0.35CoCrFeNi has limited ductility.
The initial cast alloy has coarse grains larger than 100 µm.
Slow cooling of the cast alloy creates a potential for brittle intermetallic formation.
Severe plastic deformation can refine the alloy to a grain size below 50 nm.
Annealing at 300-500°C after severe plastic deformation will retain FCC and BCC solid-solution phases without grain coarsening or intermetallic precipitation.
An SPD strain greater than 4 is sufficient or necessary to obtain the proposed nanocrystalline structure.
An inert argon atmosphere will prevent oxidation during processing.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the proposed nanocrystalline FCC+BCC solid-solution structure.
Sluggish diffusion stabilizes the refined structure and limits phase decomposition during annealing.
Severe plastic deformation increases dislocation density and grain-boundary area.
The increased grain-boundary area enhances strength through the Hall-Petch effect.
Solid-solution hardening contributes to the increased strength.
The dual-phase structure provides deformation compatibility that mitigates brittleness and retains ductility.
The proposed processing route will increase hardness and yield strength by 50-100% relative to the cast alloy.
No brittle intermetallic phases will be present after the proposed processing route.
Annealing above 600°C may cause grain coarsening or intermetallic precipitation.
Extreme Al or Ti contents favor ordered B2 phase formation.
Exact phase fractions and grain-size distributions depend on the SPD method and annealing parameters.
Formation of intermetallics or grain growth beyond 50 nm after annealing at 600°C for one hour would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The claimed processing window is 300-500°C and instability is anticipated near or above 600°C, yet the falsification test is conducted at 600°C. Failure under a condition outside the proposed stable processing window would not falsify the claim that the microstructure is stable at 300-500°C.
